title: 2010 JAMB USE OF ENGLISH QUESTIONS
subject: Use of English
instructions: COMPREHENSION: Read each passage carefully and answer the questions that follow it

questions.question: Which Use of English Paper Type is given to you?
questions.explanation: This is a standard JAMB Use of English paper format.

questions.question: According to the writer, the exciting thing about Spaceship Earth is that
options: it is not difficult to maintain
questions.explanation: The passage states that 'no instruction book came with it' which makes this the most exciting aspect.

questions.question: The absence of instruction manual in Spaceship Earth has
options: made the operation of the Spaceship Earth difficult
forced man to devise other means of travelling in spacecraft
questions.explanation: The passage indicates that the lack of instruction manual forced man to discover and learn through experimentation.

questions.question: From the passage, it can be deduced that man
options: is incapable of solving all his problems
by his nature is in constant search of knowledge
questions.explanation: The passage shows that man is naturally curious and constantly seeks to understand and discover.

questions.question: The writer's mood in the passage is that of
questions.explanation: The writer presents facts objectively without taking a strong emotional stance.

questions.question: The expression, … stress is an issue everybody can relate to experimentally, means that
options: it is better understood when experienced
its problem can be solved by everybody
questions.explanation: The phrase suggests that stress is best understood through personal experience.

questions.question: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Stress is mostly caused by internal factors
Stress can only be avoided during relaxation
Stress is better handled by the individual
The issues of stress can be solved with no effort
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that stress can be managed through relaxation techniques.

questions.question: According to the passage, the major step in controlling stress is
options: visiting family doctors for check-up and treatment
constant exercise to dissipate every energy
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes changing one's approach and attitude to stress management.

questions.question: The experts feel one can control one's stress because
options: it is not difficult to control
questions.explanation: The passage states that most stress is self-generated, giving individuals control over it.

questions.question: From the passage, it can be deduced that stress is
options: hormonal disorder in the body system
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that stress is primarily self-generated by individuals.

questions.question: According to the writer, corruption is triggered off by
questions.explanation: The passage mentions affluent living habits compared to income as an indicator of corruption.

questions.question: From the passage, one of the consequences of corruption is that
options: it is beneficial to wealth people whole stole public wealth
it impedes the progress of a nation
people get what they want with so much money to spend
questions.explanation: The passage clearly states that corruption can slow down development.

questions.question: Who, according to the writer should prevent corruption?
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes the role of government in fighting corruption and promoting good governance.

questions.question: Which of the following is an indication of ethical standard of governance?
questions.explanation: Democratic governance is mentioned as a key aspect of ethical governance standards.

questions.question: The essence of fighting corruption, according to the passage, is to
questions.explanation: The passage emphasizes that fighting corruption is crucial for promoting good governance.

questions.question: Drought is a word that invokes strong emotions. This is not surprising as the … is usually accompanied by a number of unpleasant developments.
questions.explanation: Drought is a natural phenomenon that causes unpleasant developments.

questions.question: These developments have … for all citizens, starting from the peasant farmers to the state and federal governments
questions.explanation: The developments have implications (consequences) for all citizens.

questions.question: which may be plunged into emergency and crises situations which, if not successfully … could result in social unrest.
questions.explanation: Emergency and crisis situations need to be managed to prevent social unrest.

questions.question: The timeliness of the onset of the rains in various regions of the country and their adequate distribution thereafter have become … of considerable anxiety to all people.
questions.explanation: The rain patterns have become subjects (matters) of anxiety for people.

questions.question: The fact, however, is that periodic reduction in normal … of rainfall in the country is not new.
questions.explanation: The reduction in normal supply of rainfall refers to the availability of rain.

questions.question: Since large areas of the country are drought prone, the consequences are …
questions.explanation: The consequences are inevitable (unavoidable) given the drought-prone nature of large areas.

questions.question: One has to do with emergency measures and the other with … measures.
questions.explanation: The contrast is between emergency measures and routine (regular) measures.

questions.question: In addition, where whole populations are forced to abandon their lands or pastures in search of food, there are bound to be other lasting and … consequences
questions.explanation: The consequences happen simultaneously (at the same time) with the abandonment.

questions.question: Government should provide farmers with agricultural inputs and ensure that they have easy access to these inputs under the relief …
questions.explanation: Relief scheme refers to a systematic program to provide assistance.

questions.question: Emergency measures will be much more … if a mechanism is established to ensure adequate preparedness and defence against the occurrence of drought.
questions.explanation: With proper mechanisms in place, emergency measures will be more effective.

questions.question: Though Mr. Iro is a new chairman, he views other members with jaundiced eye.
options: He takes a rather forceful position on dealing with his members
He takes an unfavourable position concerning his members
He takes a sickly view of his members
He takes a rather hazy view of his members
questions.explanation: To view with jaundiced eye means to look at something with prejudice or unfavorably.

questions.question: People are not interested in who rules.
options: People are not ruled by the leaders they want
People are not concerned about who rules them
The rulers are not concerned about the people
People who rule are not interested in the ruled
questions.explanation: The sentence means people don't care about who their rulers are.

questions.question: It was good to steer a middle course in whatever one does.
options: It is always good to get midway in anything one does
It is always good to act with moderation
It is always good to move away from the forefront
It is always good to work very hard
questions.explanation: To steer a middle course means to act with moderation, avoiding extremes.

questions.question: The witness said he had no axe to grind with his brothers
options: He had no hatred for the brothers
He had no axe and therefore stole the matchet
He had no axe and therefore borrowed their matchet
He had no vested interest in the brothers
questions.explanation: To have no axe to grind means to have no hidden agenda or personal interest in a matter.

questions.question: The footballers moved with their tails between their legs.
options: they moved happily because they won the match
they were unhappy because they had been despised by their opponents
they were ashamed because they had been defeated
they moved with their tails between their legs
questions.explanation: To move with tail between legs means to be ashamed or embarrassed, typically after a defeat.

questions.question: The headmaster managed to talk his way out of having to give a speech
options: he delivered a speech despite the difficulty
he managed to give a speech out of a difficult situation
he managed to get himself out of a difficult situation
he managed to talk on his way
questions.explanation: To talk one's way out means to use clever or persuasive speech to avoid doing something.

questions.question: As regards the matter, we have crossed the rubicon
options: we are completely at a loss
questions.explanation: To cross the Rubicon means to pass a point of no return, to be irrevocably committed to a course of action.

questions.question: Uche is full of himself
questions.explanation: To be full of oneself means to be conceited or self-important.

questions.question: As debutants in that tournament, the Super Eagles were up against their first opponents by three goals to nill
options: The Super Eagles were playing in the tournament for the first time, but they won their match by three goals to nothing
Though the Super Eagles were rated as the weakest side in the tournament, they won their first match by three goals to nill
Even though the Super Eagles were playing without some of their regulars, they won their match by three goals to nill
As the best attackers in the match, the Super Eagles easily defeated their opponents by three goals to nothing
questions.explanation: As debutants means they were playing in the tournament for the first time.

questions.question: The woman was mournful as her husband was found dead drunk
options: She was sad because of her husband was absolutely drunk
She was apprehensive that her husband would drink again as soon he recovered from the drunken stupor
She was sad because her husband was drunk and always as helpless as a dead man
She was mourning because her husband drank and died
questions.explanation: Dead drunk means extremely drunk, and the woman was sad because her husband was in such a helpless state.

questions.question: I am optimistic about the interview though it was a mind-bending exercise
questions.explanation: The opposite of mind-bending (mentally challenging) would be easy.

questions.question: The trader was amused by the cut-throat rush for the goods
questions.explanation: The opposite of cut-throat (intense competition) would be lacklustre (lacking energy or enthusiasm).

questions.question: The teacher said that Ali's essay was full of many redundant details
questions.explanation: The opposite of redundant (unnecessary) would be necessary.

questions.question: His father surmounted the myriad of obstacles on his way
questions.explanation: The opposite of myriad (countless) would be few.

questions.question: Her ingenuous smile drew our attention
questions.explanation: The opposite of ingenuous (innocent/naive) would be arrogant.

questions.question: Ndeni gave a flawless speech at the party
questions.explanation: The opposite of flawless (perfect) would be imperfect.

questions.question: Beneath Ado's guff exterior, he's really very kind-hearted
questions.explanation: The opposite of guff (rough/harsh) would be nice.

questions.question: The captain says sports is being debased by commercial sponsorship
questions.explanation: The opposite of debased (lowered in quality) would be elevated.

questions.question: Governing a country is not always as straightforward as people sometimes imagine
questions.explanation: The opposite of straightforward (simple/direct) would be complicated.

questions.question: The crowd was very receptive to the speaker's suggestion
questions.explanation: The opposite of receptive (willing to accept) would be hostile.

questions.question: There was a general acquiescence on the new drug law
questions.explanation: The opposite of acquiescence (acceptance) would be resistance.

questions.question: Aisha seems to feel ambivalent about her future
questions.explanation: The opposite of ambivalent (uncertain) would be decisive.

questions.question: The report of the committee contained a plethora of details
questions.explanation: The opposite of plethora (excess) would be shortage.

questions.question: The weather was still very heavy and sultry
questions.explanation: The opposite of sultry (hot and humid) would be cold and friendly.

questions.question: Ada gave her husband a look that made words superfluous
questions.explanation: The opposite of superfluous (excessive) would be scanty (insufficient).

questions.question: A political Impasse does not offer the best opportunity for merrymaking
questions.explanation: Impasse means a deadlock or gridlock situation.

questions.question: We were all enthusiastic as we awaited the result of the election
questions.explanation: Enthusiastic means excited and eager, similar to agitated.

questions.question: The uniform makes the guards look absurd
questions.explanation: Absurd means ridiculous or unreasonable.

questions.question: The law is often tardy in reacting to changing attitude
questions.explanation: Tardy means slow or delayed.

questions.question: Isa and llu ate sumptuous meal on their brother's wedding day
questions.explanation: Sumptuous means lavish or expensive.

questions.question: Kaltume crouched over the paper on her desk
questions.explanation: To crouch means to bend down or stoop.

questions.question: The panacea for a country's economic mess lies in systematic planning and hardwork
questions.explanation: Panacea means a cure or solution for all problems.

questions.question: Thousands of workers have been victims of retrenchment since the military came back to power
questions.explanation: Retrenchment means laying off workers, which leads to unemployment.

questions.question: The principal gave his speech offhand at the sports meeting
questions.explanation: Offhand means without preparation, done casually.

questions.question: Jankoli was dressed in an old assortment of clothes
questions.explanation: Assortment means a variety or mixture, similar to melange.

questions.question: The girl's father was astounded to see her appear from the shrine
questions.explanation: Astounded means greatly surprised or astonished.

questions.question: The director's remark was extremely apposite to the issue being discussed
questions.explanation: Apposite means appropriate or relevant.

questions.question: Her reputation is without a blemish
questions.explanation: Blemish means a fault or flaw.

questions.question: Ugo is eligible for the post of secretary
questions.explanation: Eligible means qualified or suitable.

questions.question: This is an abridged version of No Longer at Ease
questions.explanation: Abridged means shortened or condensed.

questions.question: Lemoti……… as a painter, but also as a sculptor
questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'not only...but also'.

questions.question: He can recall the important dates in the nation's history, it is interesting to listen as he rattles ………
questions.explanation: To rattle off means to recite quickly and easily.

questions.question: The boy told his mother ……..
options: that was the girl he told her about
that was the girl I told you about her
that was the girl I told her about
that is the girl he told her about
questions.explanation: This is the grammatically correct indirect speech structure.

questions.question: Last Monday his father asked me ……..
options: if I had come some days before
if I had come the day before
questions.explanation: This is the correct indirect speech structure for asking about the previous day.

questions.question: His wife was badly injured in the fracas, but I think she will pull ……..
questions.explanation: To pull through means to recover from illness or difficulty.

questions.question: A wide range of options …….. made available to students in the final year last year
questions.explanation: The subject 'range' is singular, so we use 'was'.

questions.question: One of the women who …….. in the premises ……. been ordered to quit
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with 'one' (singular), so 'sells' and 'has'.

questions.question: The new trade agreement should facilitate………
questions.explanation: This is the correct word order: more rapid economic growth.

questions.question: The principal said that he was pleased……… my effort.
questions.explanation: We use 'pleased with' to express satisfaction.

questions.question: Paper is made……. Wood pulp
questions.explanation: We use 'made from' when the original material is transformed.

questions.question: Long after everyone …….. the hall, obi still sat inside.
questions.explanation: We use past perfect 'had left' to show the sequence of events.

questions.question: They are the …….. dresses
questions.explanation: The plural possessive form of 'baby' is 'babies'.'

questions.question: The politician was sent……. Exile
questions.explanation: We use 'into exile' to express being sent away.

questions.question: When we looked up, we…….. the plane some miles away
questions.explanation: To sight means to see or observe something.

questions.question: Vital….. is still spread….. word of mouth in most villages in Africa
questions.explanation: We use 'by word of mouth' to express oral communication.

questions.question: Western education is one of the….. of colonial rule.
questions.explanation: Legacy means something handed down from the past.

questions.question: The federal government has…… child trafficking
questions.explanation: To proscribe means to forbid or ban something.

questions.question: The man was happy that his son confessed his guilt and so the others were……
questions.explanation: To exonerate means to clear from blame or accusation.

questions.question: Based on the facts before me, I have no alternative…… to hold you responsible
questions.explanation: We use 'than' after 'alternative' to introduce the other option.

questions.question: Many people would always find reasons to……the law
questions.explanation: To circumvent means to find a way around or avoid.

questions.question: Coup
questions.explanation: Coup and hoot have the same vowel sound /uː/.

questions.question: Indict
questions.explanation: Indict and bright have the same vowel sound /aɪ/.

questions.question: Roared
questions.explanation: Roared and towered have the same vowel sound /ɔː/.

questions.question: Sheath
questions.explanation: Sheath and length have the same consonant sound /θ/.

questions.question: High
questions.explanation: High and who have the same consonant sound /h/.

questions.question: Of course
questions.explanation: Of course and over have the same consonant sound /f/.

questions.question: Boys
questions.explanation: Boys and noise rhyme with the same ending sound.

questions.question: Shine
questions.explanation: Shine and fine rhyme with the same ending sound.

questions.question: Seer
questions.explanation: Seer and spare rhyme with the same ending sound.

questions.question: Political
questions.explanation: The correct stress pattern is PoLItical with stress on the second syllable.

questions.question: Satisfactory
questions.explanation: The correct stress pattern is satisFACtory with stress on the third syllable.

questions.question: captivity
questions.explanation: The correct stress pattern is capTIvity with stress on the second syllable.

questions.question: EMEKA finished his home work yesterday
options: Was Emeka helped to do his homework?
When did Emeka finish his homework?
Who finished his home work yesterday?
questions.explanation: The emphasis on EMEKA suggests the question is asking about who did it.

questions.question: Taiwo SAILED to London
questions.explanation: The emphasis on SAILED suggests the question is asking about the mode of transport.

questions.question: My bag is made of LEATHER
options: Whose bag is made of leather
Is my bag made of polythene?
Is Abu's bag made of leather?
Is my bag made of leather?
questions.explanation: The emphasis on LEATHER suggests the question is asking about the material.
